Streets, schools and getting around East Chilliwack

items.t: Highway 1 access is at the Prest Road and Annis Road interchanges per the same page; highway interchange numbers and driving commute times were not confirmed on an official source: Not verified.

The ground is planned through the City's Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500 — the city-wide plan. The Sardis neighbourhood plan is Schedule B5 of the same bylaw (never "Schedule D / Bylaw 5024"); it does not govern this area, and it is named here only so the two schedules are not confused.

Services are outside the area: the nearest City recreation centres are Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, Unit 1, 9145 Corbould Street, and Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way; the nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; the nearest hospital is Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd, Chilliwack; the nearest grocery named by the City is Save-on-Foods, 46020 Yale Road. No shopping centre inside this rural area was confirmed on an official source: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in East Chilliwack

items.t: The stratification bar (why there is no condo stock to regulate here): ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. Combined with the ALR housing caps below, this is the structural reason is a zero.

Chilliwack plan and zoning: Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500, with the Agricultural Area Plan as Schedule B1 (the Sardis plan is Schedule B5 of the same bylaw — never "Schedule D / Bylaw 5024"). Zoning is Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000: in the AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone the minimum lot area is 7.5 ha for land excluded or exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within the ALR, 1 ha for a boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha for a homesite severance or boundary adjustment approved by the Agricultural Land Commission; minimum lot width is 25 m. Smaller residential lots exist near the school and along Chilliwack Central Road, but no residential zone minimum for them was confirmed from the bylaw text: Not verified. Chilliwack's SSMUH bylaw is Bylaw 5395, adopted June 18, 2024.
Farm character the plan protects: the Agricultural Area Plan states the farm sector in the plan area is dominated by dairy and poultry operations, nurseries and greenhouses.
Wells and septic: servicing for a single parcel is not verified — verify well and septic on any rural parcel before removing subjects.

Form B (strata law, stated for completeness): Strata Property Act s. 59 — on a resale purchase the strata must provide a Form B Information Certificate stating strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and a summary of the strata's insurance, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It has no application to the freehold farm and rural parcels that make up this sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Chilliwack

items.t: The school name is older than the board name. East Chilliwack Elementary's own history page records that the East Chilliwack School District was created on April 14, 1890 after a petition to the Government, that settler Chas Brown donated one acre of land for the school, and that the present building replaced the 1949 school in 1993.

A new school may redraw the east side. The Province's capital projects page lists a new SD33 east-side elementary school under construction at 10125 McGrath Road — a three-storey school providing 500 new student spaces for grades K–5, with a neighbourhood learning centre for child care programming, an estimated project value of $58.6 million, and estimated occupancy April 2027 — which may redraw east-side catchments; verify the exact address in the locator close to purchase.

Drainage and dyking are a separate line on the tax bill. Chilliwack levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rates — a rural-buyer cost that does not appear in a municipal-rate-only comparison.
There are no SnapStats numbers for East Chilliwack — anyone quoting one is quoting nothing.

The Sardis plan number is a trap for this area too. East Chilliwack is governed by the Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of OCP Bylaw 5500; documents citing a "Schedule D" plan or Bylaw 5024 for any Chilliwack neighbourhood are citing a plan structure that does not exist in the current bylaw.

items.t: Nearby areas: downtown Chilliwack and Little Mountain to the west and northwest, Rosedale to the east, and the Cheam / Fraser River side to the north.

No market numbers exist for this area in the sources used: Chilliwack is not covered by SnapStats (neither the GVR nor the FVR September 2026 report contains a Chilliwack section or an East Chilliwack row; CADREB governs and publishes no area stats in those reports), so every market figure for East Chilliwack — inventory, solds, sales ratio, medians — is not verified, none is stated, and none is substituted from another community.

Schools named for the area (Ministry-listed names only): East Chilliwack Elementary (K–5), 49190 Chilliwack Central Road, and Cheam Elementary (K–5), 9895 Banford Road, on the provincial school list; SD33's structure is elementary K–5, middle 6–8 and secondary 9–12.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in East Chilliwack

items.t: The stratification bar (why there is no townhouse stock to regulate here): ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 239 and ALCA s. 21(1)). Combined with the ALR housing caps below, this is the structural reason is a zero.

ALR housing rules, in full three-tier farm form where farm classification is in issue: parcel-level ALR status is per address and was not confirmed for any parcel: Not verified — check the parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission mapping. Where land is in the ALR: generally no more than one residence per parcel; a principal residence built without an ALC application capped at 500 m² total floor area; and one additional detached residence up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger parcels. BC Assessment farm-classification minimum gross farm income is in full three-tier form — $10,000 (under 0.8 ha), $2,500 (0.8–4 ha), and $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area in excess of 4 ha (over 4 ha); a flat "$2,500+" statement is an error wherever it is met. Farm-sector feeds are generic — never present a feed card as a confirmed sector operation.

: rates are the sum of each taxing authority's levy, with separate rates for each property class and additional taxes levied for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rates. Notices are due the first working day after July 1 each year, with a 5% late payment penalty on taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% on taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026. The FVRD rural regime does not apply inside the City.

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata frame, for completeness): since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, no deferral by vote; a strata with fewer than five lots sits UNDER that threshold. Since Nov 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF. Rental-restriction bylaws are void since Nov 24, 2022 for strata property anywhere in BC; age bylaws: Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 allow only a 55-or-older strata residency bylaw, with exemptions expanded May 1, 2023. None of these rules creates or affects stock in this sub-area, where no strata townhouse is verified.

PTT + exemptions, with the tier flag: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2,000,000, 3% above $2,000,000, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000 — an "Over $3M — 5%" row is a compression of 3% + 2%, and worked examples must show the tier math. First-time buyers: exempt on the first $500,000 at $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000. Newly built home exemption: full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000.

blocks.text: Lots and land in East Chilliwack
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple farm and rural parcels are the only land form: typical types are rural detached houses on half-acre to multi-acre lots, hobby farms, equestrian properties, and commercial dairy, poultry, nursery and forage farms in the ALR; the Agricultural Area Plan says the farm sector in the plan area is dominated by dairy and poultry operations, nurseries and greenhouses. A parcel here is bought whole (title, farm buildings, residence rights as the ALR rules allow), not as a serviced lot in a subdivision product.
Named subdivisions / bare-land developments: none verified: No project in this sub-area was confirmed on a developer's own site: Not verified.

Lot sizes/zones: under Zoning Bylaw 2020 No. 5000, the AL zone sets a minimum lot area of 7.5 ha for land excluded or exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within the ALR, 1 ha for a boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha for a homesite severance or boundary adjustment approved by the Agricultural Land Commission; minimum lot width is 25 m. Smaller residential lots exist near the school and along Chilliwack Central Road, but no residential zone minimum for them was confirmed from the bylaw text. No typical lot size beyond the zone minimums is given.

Bare-land strata: none — and barred on ALR ground: Residences in the ALR cannot be stratified without the ALC's permission — depositing a strata plan is a subdivision, and a person must not subdivide agricultural land unless permitted by the Commission or under the ALR General Regulation (ALCA, s. 21(1); ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239).

ALR vs non-ALR split: parcel-level ALR status is per address and was not confirmed for any parcel here: Not verified — no split percentage is stated. Whether a specific parcel is in the ALR must be confirmed for that parcel, in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder and on title, before any subdivision, residence or value assumption is priced.
Strata vs freehold
Servicing: well and septic servicing for a single parcel is not verified — rural parcels are treated as a parcel-level servicing check (well record, sewerage filings) and no servicing is assumed.

Flood/diking character of the land: the City's Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 sets minimum building setbacks of 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal, and the City maintains a diking network for the Fraser and Vedder systems; Chilliwack also levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rates. Which watercourses carry parcel-level setbacks for a given East Chilliwack parcel is a per-property check: Not verified.

items.t: Its school corridor is Chilliwack Central Road: East Chilliwack Elementary is at 49190 Chilliwack Central Road, per the Province's school list.

The City classifies its neighbourhood plans as urban, hillside and rural; East Chilliwack's farmland falls under the Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of the 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP), not a standalone neighbourhood plan.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: the housing stock

items.t: The City states nearly 70% of land in Chilliwack is in the ALR and not available for development, which shapes why East Chilliwack stock stays low-density.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of OCP Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, is the plan covering East Chilliwack farmland.

Development Permit Area D-4, Farm Home Plate, requires residential buildings on valley-floor farmland to cluster in a farm home plate, leaving the balance for agriculture, where siting does not conform to zoning.

Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 applies: in standard-dike areas habitable floors must meet the flood construction level for the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers, plus 0.6 metres freeboard, unless a covenant and qualified professional's report support a waiver.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: East Chilliwack Elementary offers before/after care through Little Valley 123 Child Care, listed on SD33's early-learning site.

Fraser River flood response phases are keyed to the Mission gauge, at about 5.5 metres bankfull and 6.0 metres for minor flooding in unprotected areas, per the City flood information read in earlier work and its Flood Protection page.
Hillside land in Chilliwack is defined by the City for subdivision purposes as land with slopes of 20 percent or more — relevant only at East Chilliwack's upland edges, not the flat farm floor.
Most subdivisions require a tree and green space management plan under Tree Management (Land Development) Bylaw 2008, No. 3585, before final approval.

faq.a: School District No. 33 (SD33) transportation lists the Eastern Hillside/East Chilliwack area as East Chilliwack Elementary School, Rosedale Traditional Community School, and Chilliwack Secondary School. That three-school pathway, elementary on Chilliwack Central Road, middle in Rosedale, secondary in Chilliwack Proper, is the pattern a buyer should verify for their exact address.

In May 2026 SD33 approved splitting Cheam Elementary's catchment between Little Mountain, Strathcona and the new east-side elementary opening September 2027, and moving Rosedale Kindergarten-Grade 5 students there. East Chilliwack Elementary was not named in that decision.
faq.q: Will the new east-side elementary school change East Chilliwack catchments?

faq.a: Subdivision needs City Approving Officer approval and, inside the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) rules also apply. The City's subdivisions page lists creating two or more lots as requiring a subdivision application. Do not assume a large lot can be split until both the City zoning and ALR status are checked for that parcel.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a farm lot in East Chilliwack?

faq.a: BC Transit route 71 runs on Yale Road, north of the Chilliwack Central Road farm area, between downtown Chilliwack and Harrison Hot Springs.
